perf.summary: The Euler/Legendre exponent (mod-1)/2 is recomputed repeatedly, and the non-residue search re-divides it every iteration of the z loop.
perf.currentCost: (mod-1)/2 is computed at line 13 and again per-iteration inside InitializeTonelliShanks' while loop (line 23: ModPow.Run(z,(mod-1)/2,mod)). Each z probe is a full ModPow (~log mod modmuls); recomputing the divisor is minor, but passing the same exponent object lets it be hoisted, and the legendre check at line 13 can be reused conceptually.
perf.proposedChange: Compute long half = (mod - 1) >> 1 once (mod is positive and odd on this path so (mod-1) is even, shift == /2 exactly) and reuse it for the line-13 Legendre test and inside the z-search loop. Hoist it out of the while in InitializeTonelliShanks.
perf.rationale: Replaces repeated 64-bit division by a single shift and removes recomputation inside a loop. Small but free; the division is otherwise re-executed on every non-residue probe.
perf.risk: mod is guaranteed positive (Legendre test passed) and odd (mod%4==3 branch already returned for the 4k+3 case, and even mod cannot have these residues), so mod-1>=0 and >>1 equals /2. No signed-shift hazard since mod-1>=0.

perf.summary: Loop bound (int)(m - i - 1) is recomputed and cast on every iteration of the for loop.
perf.currentCost: for (int j = 0; j < (int)(m - i - 1); j++) re-evaluates the long subtraction m-i-1 and the long->int cast each iteration as the loop condition.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist: int bound = (int)(m - i - 1); for (int j = 0; j < bound; j++) b2 = ModMul.Run(b2,b2,mod);
perf.rationale: Removes a per-iteration 64-bit subtraction and narrowing cast from a loop whose body otherwise contains only one cheap-to-medium modmul; helps the compiler keep the bound in a register and may aid Burst unrolling.
perf.risk: None; m-i-1 is loop-invariant within this call (m and i are parameters, not mutated). Value range is small (<= s <= 62), cast is safe.

perf.summary: m carries s (a bit-count <= 62) but is typed long, forcing 64-bit arithmetic and a long->int cast in ComputeB2.
perf.currentCost: long m = s; ... m = i; passes m as long into ComputeB2 which then casts (int)(m - i - 1). All m arithmetic is 64-bit for a value that never exceeds the bit-length of mod (<=62).
perf.proposedChange: Type m as int (s is already int, i is int). Then ComputeB2 takes int m and the bound is simply m - i - 1 with no cast. Drop the long type throughout the m chain.
perf.rationale: Narrower type removes an unnecessary cast and uses 32-bit ops; mostly clarity/correctness-of-intent plus eliminating the narrowing conversion. Negligible cycles but removes a code smell and a cast in a loop condition.
perf.risk: s = popcount-of-trailing-zeros of mod-1 <= 62 for any long mod, well within int. Safe. Must update ComputeB2 signature accordingly (internal, no external callers).

perf.summary: Dead t==0 check inside the main loop; t can never become 0 once entered with a nonzero quadratic residue.
perf.currentCost: if (t == 0) return 0; is evaluated every iteration of the infinite loop. a!=0 is guaranteed by ModSqrt.Run (returns early when a==0) and mod is prime on this path, so t = a^q is a nonzero residue and stays nonzero under multiplication by units; the branch is never taken.
perf.proposedChange: Remove the t==0 guard from the loop (and the corresponding guard is redundant with the t==1 termination). Keep only if (t==1) return Min(r, mod-r).
perf.rationale: Removes one comparison+branch per Tonelli-Shanks iteration. Minor, but the inputs guarantee it is dead code under the documented unchecked contract.
perf.risk: Only safe under the precondition that mod is prime and a is a nonzero residue (already enforced by the Legendre test at line 13 and the a==0 early return). If callers may pass composite mod, t==0 could theoretically occur; keep the guard if the unchecked contract permits composite moduli. State explicitly: requires prime mod.
